title: Instrument Definition
description: An instrument is DATA, not code (BUILD.md Operating Rule 2). This contract defines a single instrument: provenance fields plus an ordered list of sections. The engine renders any definition that validates here. Scored sections carry their own scales, criterion-referenced band thresholds, a neutral construct_explainer, and tendency-language band copy. Aspirational section types carry no scoring.

id.description: Stable machine id, e.g. "bigfive". Used in record files and viewer aggregation.

version.description: Semver. The quantitative spine must stay byte-for-byte identical across sittings for comparability (DESIGN.md); bump only on a real content change.

title.description: Human-facing title shown at the top of the instrument.

source.description: Where the item pool came from (e.g. "IPIP-NEO-120"). Citation/license presence is a Layer-1 gate; transcribe, never invent (Operating Rule 3).

citation.description: Full bibliographic citation for the source pool, pointing at content-sources/<id>.md.

license.description: License of the source items (e.g. "Public Domain (IPIP)"). VIA proprietary items are forbidden; strengths uses IPIP.

intro.description: Optional framing shown before the first section.

sections.description: Ordered sections. Rendered top to bottom in a single sitting.

section.description: One of the five fixed section types, discriminated by `type`.

infoSection.description: A teaching / framing block. No scoring, no input.

body.description: Teaching copy (plain text / light markdown). Subject to the essence-language linter.

scoredLikertSection.description: Psychometric Likert section. Items load onto scales; scales sum (with reverse-keying) and map to bands. Bands are criterion-referenced by default; a section carrying `norms` and band_thresholds.mode = "norm-referenced" is scored against published norms instead, and its cuts are percentile fractions. Each scale ships a neutral construct_explainer plus per-band light/shadow/one_thing_to_try copy in tendency language.

intro.description: Optional teaching copy before the items.

anchors.description: Likert response labels in ascending order, e.g. ["Very inaccurate", ... , "Very accurate"]. The number of anchors is the response range; an item's `points` must not exceed it.

band_thresholds.description: Cut points expressed as fractions in (0,1), strictly ascending, one shorter than `bands`. In the default criterion-referenced mode they are fractions of each scale’s OWN min..max range. In norm-referenced mode they are percentile fractions against the section’s `norms`.

bands.description: Ordered band ids from lowest to highest, e.g. ["low", "balanced", "high"]. Every scale must supply per-band copy keyed by exactly these ids.

cuts.description: Fractional boundaries in (0,1), strictly ascending. Length = bands.length - 1. Default thirds = [0.3333, 0.6667].

mode.description: How `cuts` are interpreted. "norm-referenced" requires the section to carry `norms`.

copy_poles.description: Optional map from each band id to the band-copy key it uses. Lets a fine-grained band set (seven bands) share a smaller set of authored copy poles (low / mid / high). When absent, band ids and copy keys are the same.

id.description: Optional stable item id for fixtures/record raw_responses keys.

text.description: Verbatim item wording transcribed from the cited source.

scale.description: Id of the scale this item loads onto (must match a scales[].id).

reverse.description: If true, the response is reverse-keyed before summing.

points.description: Number of response options for this item; must be <= anchors.length.

scales.description: Scales this section computes, across up to four hierarchy levels. A `facet` owns items. A `domain`, `aspect`, or `metatrait` owns no items and is computed from `members`.

parent.description: Optional id of a parent domain scale this facet rolls up into.

construct_explainer.description: Neutral explanation of WHAT the construct is and what psychology understands about it. Not a verdict about the person. Tendency language only.

bands.description: Per-band copy, keyed by the band ids declared in band_thresholds.bands. Every declared band must be present (enforced by the engine/gates against band_thresholds).

level.description: Hierarchy level. Only `facet` scales carry items; the rest are composites defined by `members`.

members.description: Composite definition: the signed sum of these scales’ scores. Required for any scale above facet level.

sign.description: Direction the member enters the sum.

spectrum.description: Short labels for the two ends of this scale, shown whatever band a result lands in, so the whole spectrum is visible and not just the student’s slice of it.

reliability.description: Internal-consistency reliability for the default norm group; drives the reported uncertainty range.

marker_loadings.description: For aspects: the published factor loading of each member facet on this aspect, kept so the membership rule stays auditable.

norms.description: Published norm tables enabling norm-referenced scoring. Required when band_thresholds.mode is "norm-referenced".

source.description: Where the norm table comes from.

note.description: Any transformation applied to the published values, and which values are derived rather than published.

default_group.description: Id of the comparison group used unless the student picks another.

short.description: Compact label for the comparison-group selector.

facet_correlation.description: Average within-domain facet correlation, back-solved from the published domain and facet SDs. Used to derive composite SDs.

metatrait_correlation.description: Assumed average domain intercorrelation within each metatrait. Stated, not published — see the instrument’s content source.

scales.description: Per-scale norm statistics, keyed by scale id.

mean.description: Norm-group mean of this scale’s summed score, on this app’s 0-based response metric.

sd.description: Norm-group standard deviation of this scale’s summed score.

reliability.description: Internal-consistency reliability used for the standard error of measurement.

scoredMatrixSection.description: Construction-based figural matrix reasoning section. A response selects from 20 construction elements and is correct only when it exactly matches the source solution.

difficulty.description: Published 2PL item threshold (b), or null for the one misfitting item.

discrimination.description: Published 2PL item discrimination (a), or null for the one misfitting item.

calibrated.description: False excludes the item from scored random forms.

bandCopy.description: Tendency-language copy for one band of one scale. 'No trait is bad': every band has a light side and a shadow, plus one concrete nudge.

light.description: The upside / where this tendency helps.

shadow.description: Where this tendency can get in the way.

one_thing_to_try.description: One concrete, optional experiment to push against it.

selfRatingSection.description: Student rates themselves on named dimensions. Aspirational/qualitative: no psychometric scales, no bands. Responses are stored verbatim in the record.

anchors.description: Optional labels for the rating range.

selectAndCommitSection.description: Student selects from offered options and commits. Used by the aspirational learner-profile module. No scoring. Options may map to an official IB attribute so each reframe stays defensible.

ib_attribute.description: Official IB learner-profile attribute this option maps back to (keeps subversive reframes defensible to colleagues/parents).

reframe.description: Optional 'subversive then constructive' framing copy for this option.

freeReflectionSection.description: An open writing prompt. The student authors the meaning; their text becomes the student_snapshot stored in the record (DESIGN.md read-out model C). No machine-generated prose about the person.

is_snapshot.description: If true, this section's text is the canonical student_snapshot for the record. At most one per instrument.

sectionId.description: Section id, unique within the instrument.
